_comment: The agent harness configuration. ONE file, two readers (config.ps1 for the
scripts, config.py for the Mattermost bridge), so a value is never defined
twice in two languages. Precedence, resolved only in the loaders:
built-in defaults < this file < harness.local.json (gitignored) < environment
This file is committed and MUST NOT contain secrets - it holds policy and
topology only. Machine-specific or experimental overrides go in

extension._why_locked: operator 2026-08-28: the surface the operator drives interactively must never silently degrade to a weaker model.

mattermost._note: switchable in a thread with 'profile: <name>', the same shape as the existing 'model:' and 'worktree:' directives.

claude-code._note: a Claude Code agent - a subagent in an editor session, or 'claude -p' spawned by the bridge. Model names are CLI aliases, not API ids.

little-coder._note: the local substrate: little-coder reaches llama-cpp through LiteLLM. Dispatched by dispatch.ps1 (Invoke-HarnessTask).
_why_lease: Focusing this runner WIPES its workspace and a task runs arbitrary commands in it,
so a dispatch is a live-plane mutation. dispatch.ps1's Assert-RunnerLease refuses
unless the named lease is held BY THE CALLER (lease.ps1 -Acquire -Name coder).
A runner without this key needs no lease - the policy lives here, not in the code.
Added 2026-08-30: the code claimed 'callers take the coder lease' in a comment while
nothing acquired, asserted or checked one.
_why_docker_exec: This runner declared endpoint 'http://127.0.0.1:8090' until 2026-08-30. That door did
so `curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/health` from the host is connection-refused while
`docker exec little-coder curl http://localhost:8090/health` answers. Nothing called
it, so nothing noticed. base_url is therefore CONTAINER-LOCAL and only meaningful
The port stays unpublished deliberately: daemon.py's own header says 'It is NOT the
task-trigger authentication surface; that is lc-mcpo', and lc-mcpo was retired
2026-08-20 - so POST /tasks (arbitrary agent execution) and POST /admin/shutdown are
unauthenticated. Reaching them through `docker exec` needs Docker access, which is
already an admin-equivalent boundary; publishing them on the host loopback would hand
them to every process on the machine for no capability the harness needs.
REVERT: set transport to 'http', base_url to 'http://127.0.0.1:8090', and add
dispatch.ps1's Invoke-LcApi already implements the http transport.

all-cloud._desc: the default everywhere; all three roles on cloud opus

all-local._desc: no cloud calls at all; needs the inference plane healthy

local-work-cloud-review._desc: cheap production, expensive judgement - the reviewer is the last gate before a merge

cloud-work-local-test._desc: expensive production, cheap verification - useful when the test plan is mechanical

pipeline._note: the role -> state -> duty table stays in queue.ps1: it is behavior, not tuning. Turning a gate off here is an operator decision with a real cost, which is why both are listed explicitly rather than assumed.

_env_files_note: Runtime files a worktree needs but git will not materialize. The two recipe
.env files live INSIDE the OB1 submodule, so a fresh worktree clone never has
them and `docker compose -f OB1/docker/docker-compose.yml config` fails there
while passing in the main checkout - which is how the offline harness came to
fail only in worktrees. An ARRAY of lines, like _comment above: a JSON string
cannot contain a raw newline, and the first version of this note did. PowerShell
ConvertFrom-Json accepted it; Python json.loads did not - and this file has BOTH
readers (config.ps1 and config.py), so it would have broken the bridge alone.
